transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-10-25
Start: 15:30 PT
Duration: ~52 minutes
Recording: yes
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Avery Cole (Redwood SE), Carlos Mendez (Argentum Head of IT), Sofia Alvarez (Argentum SecOps), Elena Park (Argentum Cloud Architect), Devon Price (Argentum Compliance), Marta Ruiz (Argentum Identity Engineer)

Summary: Quick security scratch review focused on SSO (SAML) + SCIM provisioning patterns, RBAC/least-privilege role model, audit logging retention, and encryption/KMS options for a Private/VPC deployment. Customer has SOC2 readiness work and wants to understand least-privilege mapping before a pilot.

Topics: SAML attribute mapping; SCIM provisioning cadence; role hierarchy and 'just enough privilege' patterns; audit log granularity and retention; KMS/HSM requirements; data residency considerations for EU shipments; fallback patterns for hosted vs. dedicated.

Transcript:
[00:00] Jordan: all right, good afternoon everyone, thanks for taking time. um quick intros, i'm Jordan, i'm the AE on the account. Priya and Avery are our solutions folks who will take us through the technical pieces.
[00:14] Carlos: hi Jordan, thanks. i'm Carlos, head of it at Argentum. Sofia and Elena are here from security and cloud. we've got about 45 minutes but open to 60 if needed.
[00:28] Priya: thanks, quick agenda — we want to cover SAML connector patterns, SCIM provisioning expectations, then walk through RBAC templates and logging/encryption Qs, and leave 10–15 for next steps. Sound ok?
[00:38] Sofia: yep that's perfect. we really want clarity on "least privilege" and how role mapping is going to work with our existing AD groups.
[00:47] Priya: great, i'll start with SAML. Redwood supports SP-initiated SAML with both Okta and Azure AD. you can map nameID or email as the subject, and we accept standard attributes for groups. one thing we often recommend is group-claim based mapping instead of relying on single attribute values — it's more maintainable.
[01:09] Marta: quick question, we do SCIM provisioning today for apps. do you support incremental SCIM updates or full syncs only?
[01:15] Avery: good question — our SCIM endpoint accepts incremental updates (PATCH) and full replace. in practice the provisioning cycle depends on your IdP — Okta pushes deltas, Azure AD can do full or delta depending on connector. note — sometimes Azure will rename attributes and that trips the mapping, so we recommend a short test org first.
[01:37] Elena: and for role semantics, do you recommend mapping to our AD groups directly, or using an intermediate attribute?
[01:43] Priya: we usually recommend an intermediate layer — SCIM->Redwood role bindings — because it gives you flexibility if you want to change role permissions later without changing AD. essentially AD group -> SCIM group -> Redwood role. the role binding table we sent last week is a starting point.
[02:03] Carlos: about least-privilege, our compliance team (Devon) is worried about too-broad admin scopes. how granular can roles be?
[02:11] Devon: yeah we need separate scopes for data export, model override, and billing. billing folks should not be able to view logs with payloads.
[02:21] Priya: absolutely. Redwood supports arbitrary role definitions with permission sets. common split is: Viewer (read-only dashboards, no raw transcripts), Operator (start/stop deployments, no billing), Auditor (view audit logs but redacted PII), Billing Admin (billing + invoices only), Security Admin (full audit and export rights). you can also set resource-scoped roles: per-environment or per-model.
[02:51] Sofia: can you redact transcripts in audit logs? we can't have customer PII in logs stored in plain text.
[02:58] Avery: yes — we offer configurable log redaction filters and tokenization for payloads. for Private customers you can push logs to your SIEM and apply your own retention. we support event-level masking and we can redact message content before it hits our audit store if you require that.
[03:18] Marta: KMS — does Redwood let us bring our own keys (BYOK) and integrate with HSM? we need FIPS 140-2/HSM backed keys.
[03:26] Priya: BYOK is supported for Private/VPC deployments. we integrate with customer KMS via standard protocols. HSM-backed keys are supported depending on the KMS (we've done Azure Key Vault and AWS CloudHSM in previous pilots). for hosted customers we offer managed encryption but for Argentum's compliance it sounds like BYOK is preferable.
[03:45] Jordan: just to clarify, in hosted mode keys are managed by Redwood; in Private you bring keys or link to your KMS. we can also do a hybrid where data at rest in storage is customer-managed.
[03:58] Elena: data residency — we have EU shipment records and need them stored in EU at rest. can you pin data region for a model or route requests to EU only?
[04:06] Priya: yes, we support region pinning. requests from EU can be routed to EU-hosted instances; for Private you'll deploy into your EU VPC. routing policies can include geo restrictions and fallback.
[04:20] Carlos: let's talk about audit logs retention — we want 7 years for certain exports per our policy. what are your retention capabilities and costs?
[04:28] Avery: we have adjustable retention policies; default is 90 days for verbose logs, you can archive to customer S3/GCS with lifecycle rules. long retention is an archive pattern — usually we push to customer-controlled cloud buckets to avoid high costs on our side. there is an add-on if you want Redwood-managed long-term retention.
[04:50] Sofia: If we route logs to our SIEM, how do you handle identity attribution? we need to tie events to SAML principals for audit trails.
[04:58] Priya: all events include SAML principal ID, session ID, and request trace id. we also emit correlation ids that your SIEM can index. for privacy we can truncate payloads but keep the correlation metadata.
[05:12] Carlos: can you walk through a role mapping example for our 'shipments-admin' group? so they can trigger reruns but not see raw customer PII.
[05:21] Priya: sure. example: AD group shipments-admin -> SCIM group 'shipments-admin' -> Redwood role 'shipments-operator'. permissions for shipments-operator: call generation endpoints, start reruns, view high-level logs (metadata only), but redact message content. no access to billing or export. we'll show mapping in the spreadsheet.
[05:43] Marta: is there a way to do just-in-time elevation for engineers who need temporary access to unredacted logs?
[05:49] Avery: yes — we have time-bound elevation flows integrated with SSO and approval hooks. you can require 2-person approval or ticketing integration. elevated sessions are recorded and flagged in audit logs.
[06:04] Devon: what's the model for emergency access? we need a break-glass account but auditable.
[06:10] Priya: break-glass accounts are supported, and we recommend MFA plus additional alerting. break-glass actions are logged and can trigger a live notification to your on-call.
[06:22] Carlos: on the network side, our legal team insists on private endpoints. can the Private deployment run inside our VPC with no public egress?
[06:30] Jordan: yes Private runs in your VPC. we can disable public egress and provide an admin bastion for maintenance. there are some careful steps for kernel-level updates but we do coordinate and provide signed packages.
[06:46] Elena: for SCIM provisioning, we want deprovisioning to remove access but not delete logs or historical artifacts. is that default?
[06:53] Priya: correct — deprovisioning removes access and can optionally anonymize or retain historical records. by default logs are retained per retention policy; we can also quarantine records that were authored by that user.
[07:06] Sofia: what about continuous monitoring? do you publish evidence for SOC 2 — like test results or control coverage?
[07:12] Jordan: we can provide a SOC 2 Type II report under NDA and a control matrix that maps Redwood controls to your requirements. for ISO we have scoping notes and can share the certificate if you need it.
[07:26] Devon: any known gaps relative to our environment? we're running air-gapped build pipelines for certain clients.
[07:33] Avery: for air-gapped builds we support an on-prem bundle. it requires some manual updates and we typically scope it as a Private on-prem deployment. there are tradeoffs: more maintenance and slower patch cadence, but you get full control.
[07:51] Carlos: latency vs cost — we may want Dedicated GPU pools for heavy inference. any security differences there?
[07:58] Priya: Dedicated pools are isolated for performance and tenancy; security controls are similar but for Dedicated we can provide stronger network isolation and dedicated keying. hosted shared environments have additional multi-tenant controls.
[08:14] Jordan: switching gears, let's do a quick walkthrough of the role mapping spreadsheet — Priya do you want to share?
[08:19] Priya: yep i'm sharing screen now — ok first tab is AD -> SCIM -> Redwood role. second tab has column for 'allowed endpoints' and 'redaction level'. for example shipments-operator has endpoints: generate, rerun, status; redaction level: metadata-only.
[08:37] Elena: can we add a column to specify who can request elevation and who approves?
[08:42] Priya: yes we've added 'elevation approver groups' as a column.
[08:46] Marta: small nit — we've seen systems where SCIM group names overflow length limits. what's the limit?
[08:52] Avery: we support SCIM names up to 256 chars but recommend keeping them under 64 for compatibility.
[08:59] Carlos: about encryption in transit — do you support mutual TLS for internal endpoints?
[09:03] Priya: mTLS is supported inside Private deployments. we can require client certs for service-to-service. for hosted we support TLS 1.2/1.3 with strong ciphers.
[09:15] Devon: audit trail integrity — can logs be signed or write-once read-many (WORM) to meet e-discovery?
[09:23] Avery: you can write logs to a WORM-capable bucket in your cloud provider and we can include signature metadata. for hosted-managed logs we have tamper-evident chains but long-term legal WORM is best on your cloud storage.
[09:40] Sofia: competitor question — some vendors have inline de-identification that uses model-side tokenization. do you do de-id inline or only post-process?
[09:49] Priya: we can do both. inline de-identification at ingestion is ideal; we also provide post-process anonymization for archived logs. both approaches can be combined.
[10:04] Carlos: ok, last thing — pilot scope. we'd like to run a VPC private pilot ingesting EU shipment data, SCIM from Azure AD, and test role mapping and redaction. can you lay out the steps?
[10:15] Jordan: yes recommended pilot plan: 1) sign pilot NDA and SOW, 2) initial scoping call to enumerate AD groups and models, 3) deploy Private instance in your EU VPC with BYOK integration, 4) run end-to-end tests (SCIM join, SAML SSO, redaction), 5) run performance smoke tests and review logs/audit. target timeline ~3 weeks once pilot SOW is signed.
[10:41] Elena: estimated cost for a 3-week pilot?
[10:45] Jordan: we'll send a slim estimate — usually there's a modest infra pass-through plus a Professional Services day rate for setup; we'll include that in the SOW.
[10:57] Sofia: anything that would block us from doing BYOK + HSM?
[11:01] Priya: technically no blocker; we just need to verify your KMS provider and whether HSM integration requires additional networking. we'll validate during the scoping step.
[11:12] Carlos: thanks — this is helpful. can you also confirm how SAML session timeouts map to Redwood sessions? we don't want long-lived sessions in case of device compromise.
[11:20] Priya: Redwood honors IdP session lifetimes; we also support session revocation via SCIM token invalidation. you can set short session TTLs at the IdP and require reauth for sensitive endpoints.
[11:33] Devon: please add a note to the role mapping that Billing Admin is strictly isolated from Auditor by default.
[11:38] Priya: will do.
[11:40] Jordan: ok let's recap next steps. we'll send the SOC2/ISO artifacts, Priya will produce role mapping sheet and sample SCIM payloads, Marta will share AD group names, Carlos will get internal signoff for pilot, and Jordan will draft the pilot SOW and estimate.
[11:58] Carlos: perfect. thanks everyone.
[12:01] Jordan: thanks all — we'll follow up by Wednesday with the docs.

Questions raised during call:
- Can Redwood perform inline de-identification? (yes, and post-process options)
- Does Redwood support BYOK/HSM? (yes for Private/VPC)
- How is audit log retention/archival handled? (configurable; recommend export to customer bucket)
- Are elevation/approval flows available? (yes, with approval hooks and time-bound sessions)
